summary: Dipak Kumar Barua was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who taught Saswati Mutsuddy. At the University of Calcutta, he was an Assistant Lecturer in Pali (attested 1979) and Dean in 1987, later serving as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara around 1996.

Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He was a lecturer at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1966) and later served at the University of Calcutta's Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture (attested 1994).

Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian and philosopher who studied at Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (PhD). He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1985–1995) and became Lawrence A. Kimpton Distinguished Service Professor in history at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who earned his M.A. and doctorate at Leiden University. He served as a lecturer (1967) and Chair of Indian History (1971–2003) at Leiden University, and founded the European Association for South Asian Studies.

Ditte Bandini-König is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, history, and archaeology. She was a visiting fellow at Collège de France (1992–1993) and a staff member at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Diwakar Acharya, a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, studied under Ramananda Giri and earned his PhD under Albrecht Wezler at the University of Hamburg. He held posts at Kyoto University (2006–2016) and became a Professor at the University of Oxford in 2016.
Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu around 1884. He served as abbot at Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Dmitry Kudryavsky was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St. Petersburg University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev from around 1886 to 1890. He held a post at the University of Tartu from around 1898 to 1918.
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar and teacher. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (~1944–1959), and taught Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen, among others.

Dominic Goodall is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and studied with Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He held a Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford, and taught at École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2005.

Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Virginia under David F. Germano, Karen Christina Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chönam, later holding a post at Utah State University (attested 2017).

Dominik Haas is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Marion Rastelli. He has held positions as a DOC Fellow at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia and at the University of Vienna (attested 2022).

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist and historian educated at the University of London and University of Oxford. He held long-term posts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine and UCL, followed by research posts at the University of Vienna and University of Alberta.

Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, beginning around 1987, and taught Edward John Garrett.
Dominique-Sila Khan was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University. She served as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don A. Pittman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who pursued doctoral studies at the University of Chicago. He served on the faculty at Texas Christian University (attested 2001).

Don Handelman is a scholar of religious studies and anthropology who studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester. He served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from around 1972 to 2007.

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe was an Indologist and historian who studied at Richmond College and under Wilhelm Geiger at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg. He served as epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (~1899–1929) and worked at the University of London (~1918–1936).

Donald A. Ringe is a linguist and Indologist who earned an MPhil at Oxford and a PhD at Yale under Warren Cowgill. After teaching Classics at Bard College (1983–1985), he joined the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.
